full_article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a tunnel at a hydropower plant Friday, raising hopes of reaching dozens of others believed to be trapped nine days after deadly floods swept away villages and submerged the Himalayan region in mud and debris.

Search teams first heard voices from inside the tunnel in the morning, allowing them to locate the two men, Nepalese lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane said. Images showed a rescuer carrying one of the workers, covered in mud, on his back, while soldiers on either side helped.

One of those rescued said more people are alive inside the tunnel, according to army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, and the search is ongoing.

“I can’t explain what we are feeling at the moment. We are just grateful to god,” Amir Maharjan, the brother of one of those rescued, told The Associated Press.

Basnet confirmed the first trapped worker’s rescue, and Neupane posted about the second on his Facebook page shortly after.

Both men were flown to a hospital in Kathmandu, and Maharjan said his family was on its way there. One of the survivors was in critical condition, according to a statement from the prime minister’s office.

Officials identified the men as a mechanical foreman and a mechanical supervisor. They were rescued from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A plant.

Nepal’s Communication Minister Bikram Timilsina wrote on his Facebook page that officials “are waiting for the rescue of more and more people.”

At least 1,287 people were killed in the Aug. 26 floods, likely caused by a glacier collapse , and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to the country’s disaster management agency. China said late Wednesday that 21 people were killed and 541 were missing on the Tibet side of the border.

Nepal’s disaster agency estimated Friday that flooding caused at least 387.5 billion Nepalese rupees ($2.5 billion) in damage to infrastructure and property.

full_article:
When a rock and ice avalanche roared down the Tibet-Nepal border on the morning of August 26, it engulfed homes, roads, villages, and markets in Rasuwa district. The floodwaters spread to the Nuwakot, and Lalitpur districts in Nepal. Green hillsides transformed into vast stretches of mud, rock, and debris. In a span of a few hours, the floods transformed river valleys; shifting and expanding them up to six times.

The NDTV team analysed satellite images by Vantor, Planet Labs PBC, Google Earth, and Google Open Buildings to understand the changing course of the Trishuli river, which carried the bulk of the devastating slurry.

From 65 metres to 443 metres.



In just hours, Nepal's floods transformed entire river valleys.



Using before-and-after satellite imagery, @NDTV Datafy tracked how the Trishuli River and its tributaries widened, shifted course and consumed large stretches of land across Nuwakot,… pic.twitter.com/OmiiAnKFBS — Rahul Kanwal (@rahulkanwal) September 3, 2026

The Nepal Army, in a statement, said that the sudden rise in water levels caused heavy damage in the Timure and Syabrubesi areas of Rasuwa district, about 125 kilometres from the Tibetan border, and the satellite images are a testimony of that.

In Timure, a border town in Rasuwa District of northern Nepal, the Trishuli River swelled over four times in its original width. Before the deadly floods, the river was 78 metres wide. After the August 26 floods, the river expanded to 350 metres.

In Syabrubesi, the river flowed with a width of 65 metres. The devastating floods stretched the river to 300 metres wide. Here, the ravaging waters are believed said to have swallowed nearly 300 homes.

Similar scenes have been witnessed in Nuwakot, one of the three worst affected districts in Nepal. In Nuwakot's Chaupthoke locality, the river bulged up to six times -- from flowing 65 metres wide before the floods to 443 metres after.

In Battar area of Nuwakot district, the river widened from 91 meters before the floods to 309 metres after.

The rescue operations in Nepal have entered their tenth day. Two workers trapped inside the Trishuli-3 'A' Hydropower Project tunnel were rescued alive today with experts calling it nothing short of a miracle.

Over 1,200 people have been reported dead, while 5,083 people are still missing in Nepal. In China, state media say 21 people have been killed, and 541 people are missing.

That takes the overall toll to 1,280 deaths, with 5,624 people missing.

full_article:
LONDON -- Two people have been rescued from a hydropower tunnel at the Trishuli 3A construction site, Nepal's Army confirmed Friday after posting videos and images from the scene on Facebook.

Nepalese lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane, an engineer who has been involved in the search operations, also posted about the two rescues on his Facebook page, including photos and videos from the scene.

He identified the two workers rescued as Sanjay Sah and Kabir Maharjan.

In an earlier Facebook post, Neupane said rescuers had heard voices from people trapped inside the tunnel.

"It has been confirmed that more than one person's voice has been heard from inside," Neupane wrote in the post. "When the rescue team said, 'Don't panic, we are rescuing,' a response of 'yes' was received from inside."

At least 557 workers are missing from the Trishuli 3A hydropower projects along the Trishuli River, with about 115 believed to be trapped in the tunnel, according to the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal.

Nepal's Communication Minister Bikram Timilsina said officials remain hopeful that more workers will be rescued. "We are waiting for the rescue of more and more people," Timilsina wrote on his Facebook page.

The death toll following last week's unprecedented flash flood at the Nepal-Tibet border has climbed to 1, 287, with an additional 4,216 people believed to still be missing as of Thursday, officials said.

Those figures increased from 1,114 deaths and 3,916 missing people, respectively, a day earlier, according to Nepal's National Disaster Management Authority.

Members of a search and rescue team work to remove the body (not pictured) of a person who was trapped inside a tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-3A Hydropower Project following devastating floods and mudslides that struck the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa, Nepal, September 4, 2026. Apf Nepal/via Reuters

Chinese state media have reported an additional 16 deaths and 546 missing people in Tibet, bringing the total death toll to 1,268 and the number of missing people on both sides of the border to 4,762.

Relief and rescue efforts are continuing, with almost all communication towers restored and nearly 12,000 people rescued through international and domestic aid.

Additionally, almost 21,500 security personnel have been mobilized in an effort to speed up search and rescue operations, with more than 5,000 people receiving treatment for injuries, officials said.

Nepali Prime Minister Shah said earlier this week that his government would begin focusing on "rehabilitation" as the length of time since the initial disaster grows.

लंदन : त्रिशुली 3 ए निर्माण स्थल पर जलविद्युत सुरंग स दू गोटे के बचाओल गेल अछि, नेपाल के सेना शुक्रदिन फेसबुक पर घटनास्थल के वीडियो आ छवि पोस्ट केलाक बाद पुष्टि केलक अछि।

खोज अभियान मे लागल अभियंता नेपाली विधायक श्री राम न्यौपाने सेहो अपन फेसबुक पेज पर दुनू बचाव के बारे मे पोस्ट केलनि जाहि मे घटनास्थल के फोटो आ वीडियो सेहो शामिल अछि।

ओ बचाओल गेल दूनू मजदूर के संजय साह आ कबीर महर्जन के रूप मे चिन्हित केलथि।

एहि सं पहिने फेसबुक पोस्ट मे न्यूपाने कहलनि जे, सुरंग के अंदर फंसल लोक के आवाज सुनल गेल अछि बचावकर्मी.

न्यूपाने पोस्ट मे लिखलनि जे, ई पुष्टि भ गेल अछि जे भीतर स एक स बेसी व्यक्ति क आवाज सुनबा मे आयल अछि। "जखन बचाव टीम कहलक जे घबराउ नहि, हम बचाव क रहल छी' त भीतर स 'हाँ' क जवाब भेटल।"

त्रिशूली नदीक कात मे त्रिशूली 3ए जलविद्युत परियोजना स कम स कम 557 मजदूर लापता अछि, जाहि मे करीब 115 मजदूर सुरंग मे फंसल हेबाक आशंका अछि नेपालक स्वतंत्र विद्युत उत्पादक संघ जनौलक अछि ।

नेपालके संचार मन्त्री बिक्रम तिमिलसिना आरो मजदुरके उद्धार होबयके अधिकारीसब आशा बनल रहल बतौलनि । तिमिलसिना अपन फेसबुक पेज पर लिखलनि जे, हम सब बेसी स बेसी लोक के बचाव के इंतजार क रहल छी।

नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा पर पिछला सप्ताह अभूतपूर्व आकस्मिक बाढ़ि के बाद मृतक के संख्या 1,287 भ गेल अछि, जखन कि गुरुवार तक अतिरिक्त 4,216 लोक के लापता मानल जा रहल अछि, अधिकारी सब कहलनि।

लोकप्रिय पढ़ै छै लिंडसे क्लैंसी ट्रायल: तनाव भड़क गेलै, कैन्हेंकि रक्षा न॑ गतिरोध के लेलऽ १ ज्यूरी क॑ दोषी ठहराबै छै १४ घंटा पहलें ईरान लाइव अपडेट: ट्रंप न॑ लुटनिक क॑ बहाना बनाबैत॑ कहलकै कि ईरान युद्ध म॑ कोनो अमेरिकी मौत नै होलै १३ घंटा पहलें ‘डांसिंग विद द स्टार’ न॑ २ दिन पहलें नयका सेलेब कलाकार आरू ओकरऽ प्रो पार्टनर के खुलासा करलकै

नेपालक राष्ट्रीय आपदा प्रबंधन प्राधिकरणक अनुसार ओ आंकड़ा एक दिन पहिने क्रमशः 1,114 मृत्यु आ 3,916 लापता छल।

नेपाल केरऽ रसुवा म॑ ४ सितम्बर २०२६ क॑ भोटेकोशी नदी प॑ आबी गेलऽ विनाशकारी बाढ़ आरू कीचड़ केरऽ स्खलन के बाद अपर त्रिशुली-३ए जलविद्युत परियोजना म॑ सुरंग के भीतर फंसलऽ एगो व्यक्ति केरऽ शव (चित्र म॑ नै) हटाबै के काम करै छै ।अपफ नेपाल/वाया रायटर

राहत आरू बचाव केरऽ प्रयास जारी छै, जेकरा म॑ लगभग सब संचार टावर क॑ बहाल करी देलऽ गेलऽ छै आरू अंतरराष्ट्रीय आरू घरेलू सहायता के माध्यम स॑ लगभग १२,००० लोगऽ क॑ बचालऽ गेलऽ छै ।

title: EU sends more aid to Nepal as flood survivors face severe humanitarian conditions - civil-protection-humanitarian-aid.ec.europa.eu
description: EU sends more aid to Nepal as flood survivors face severe humanitarian conditions  civil-protection-humanitarian-aid.ec.europa.eu
publisher.title: civil-protection-humanitarian-aid.ec.europa.eu
full_article:
As families across Nepal face the human toll of one of the country's deadliest floods in decades, the EU is adding to the relief effort led by Nepalese authorities and humanitarian partners. A first EU humanitarian air bridge flight is delivering 82 tonnes of essential supplies, while the European Commission is providing a further €500,000 for response and coordinating further help offered by European countries.

Organised with UNICEF, the Air Bridge flight has landed this morning carrying supplies for nutrition, health, water and sanitation, shelter, education and protection from EU stocks. The additional €500,000 will be channelled through the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies' disaster response emergency fund, allowing local teams to cover urgent needs. Separately, through the EU civil protection mechanism, Luxembourg, Germany, Latvia and Norway are sending equipment including life jackets, hygiene and kitchen kits, blankets, medical supplies, protective equipment and emergency energy equipment.

This further assistance builds on the EU response already underway. On 28 August, the Commission allocated €2 million in emergency humanitarian aid, on top of almost €3 million already allocated to Nepal in 2026 for disaster preparedness. EU-funded partners have been providing assistance on the ground, while Copernicus emergency satellite mapping has been activated and the EU Rapid Response and Logistic Coordinators for Asia are deployed.

Commissioner for Crisis Management Hadja Lahbib said:

‘In a single night, rivers of mud and water swept away what generations had built: homes, schools, entire communities. Nepal has suffered a devastating loss of life, and thousands of families are facing the unimaginable. The grief is only beginning to sink in. Europe stands with the Nepalese people. We are supporting emergency responders and getting emergency aid to those who need it: clean water, medicine for hospitals, shelter for families sleeping in the open, and psychological support for the grieving. European solidarity crosses oceans. We will help Nepal not just survive this tragedy, but rebuild. Stronger and never alone.’

Background

The European Commission's emergency response coordination centre operates 24/7; it ensures rapid deployment of emergency support and acts as a coordination hub between all EU Member States, the 10 additional participating states, the affected country, and civil protection and humanitarian aid experts.

यूनिसेफ के साथ आयोजित एयर ब्रिज केरऽ ई उड़ान आय सुबह पोषण, स्वास्थ्य, पानी आरू स्वच्छता, आश्रय, शिक्षा आरू ईयू केरऽ स्टॉक स॑ सुरक्षा लेली आपूर्ति लेली उतरलऽ छै । अतिरिक्त ५ लाख यूरो क॑ इंटरनेशनल फेडरेशन आफ रेड क्रॉस आरू रेड क्रिसेंट सोसाइटी केरऽ आपदा प्रतिक्रिया आपातकालीन कोष के माध्यम स॑ चैनलित करलऽ जैतै, जेकरा स॑ स्थानीय टीमऽ क॑ तत्काल जरूरतऽ क॑ पूरा करै के अनुमति मिलतै । अलग-अलग यूरोपीय संघ कें नागरिक सुरक्षा तंत्र कें माध्यम सं लक्समबर्ग, जर्मनी, लातविया आ नॉर्वे लाइफ जैकेट, स्वच्छता आ किचन किट, कंबल, चिकित्सा आपूर्ति, सुरक्षा उपकरण आ आपातकालीन ऊर्जा उपकरण सहित उपकरण भेज रहल छै.

संकट प्रबंधन आयुक्त हडजा लहबीब कहलनि जे.

‘एकहि राति मे थाल-कादो आ पानिक नदी जे पीढ़ी-दर-पीढ़ी बनौने छल: घर, स्कूल, पूरा समुदाय, ओकरा बहरा गेल। नेपाल के जान के भयावह नुकसान भेल अछि, आ हजारों परिवार के अकल्पनीय के सामना करय पड़ि रहल अछि. दुख एखनहि डूबय लागल अछि, यूरोप नेपाली जनताक संग ठाढ़ अछि। हम आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रियाकर्ताक कें समर्थन कयर रहल छी आ जरूरत कें लोगक कें आपातकालीन सहायता द रहल छी: साफ पानी, अस्पतालक कें लेल दवाई, खुला मे सुतय वाला परिवारक कें लेल आश्रय, आ शोक संतप्त लोगक कें लेल मनोवैज्ञानिक सहायता. यूरोपीय एकजुटता महासागर पार करैत अछि। हम नेपाल के सिर्फ एहि त्रासदी स बचय मे मदद करब, बल्कि पुनर्निर्माण मे मदद करब। मजबूत आ कहियो असगर नहि।’

पृष्ठभूमि

यूरोपीय आयोग केरऽ आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया समन्वय केंद्र 24/7 संचालित होय छै; इ आपातकालीन सहायता कें तेजी सं तैनाती सुनिश्चित करयत छै आ यूरोपीय संघ कें सबटा सदस्य राज्यक, 10 अतिरिक्त भाग लेवय वाला राज्यक, प्रभावित देश, आ नागरिक सुरक्षा आ मानवीय सहायता विशेषज्ञक कें बीच समन्वय केंद्र कें रूप मे काज करयत छै.

title: Is Nepal a Turning Point in Climate Coverage? - The New Republic
description: Is Nepal a Turning Point in Climate Coverage?  The New Republic
publisher.title: The New Republic
full_article:
Meanwhile, The Guardian, Agence France-Presse, The New York Times, the Associated Press, Bloomberg, Deutsche Welle, and other outlets whose reporting has long reflected established climate science suddenly are no longer outliers. The shift is particularly striking among U.S. television networks, whose climate coverage had declined by 35 percent during the first year of President Donald Trump’s second term.

NBC News did not mince words in an August 28 report, with graphics that spelled out the climate connection: “Past 60 Years Glacial Loss increased 4X, Glaciers Less Stable Worldwide From Melting.” Even CBS News has noted, more than once, the climate connection to the Nepal disaster. This despite a president, Bari Weiss, who has fired the entire CBS News climate unit, derided climate change in newsroom meetings as “woke,” and intervened to push the network’s reporting to the right on a range of topics, above all Israel. Referring to the “glacial burst” that triggered the gargantuan flood that swept away buildings, roads, and bridges, the CBS Evening News stated on August 26, “Experts believe this is linked to climate change.” On August 31, CBS’s morning news show interviewed scientist Daniel Swain while graphics told viewers, “Climate Change Impacting Extreme Weather Events, Shifting Global Sea Levels, Ecosystems, and Human Health.”

title: CT woman’s relative barely escaped deadly flooding in Nepal. She is helping family rebuild in ‘dire situation’ - Hartford Courant
description: CT woman’s relative barely escaped deadly flooding in Nepal. She is helping family rebuild in ‘dire situation’  Hartford Courant
publisher.title: Hartford Courant
full_article:
Bridgeport resident Denisha Moktan received a tearful phone call from her mother on Aug. 26 about massive flooding in their native Nepal. Their thoughts immediately turned to the nearly two dozen family members they have living in Trishuli Bazaar.

Moktan soon learned that three of her relative homes were washed away by the rushing water of the Trishuli River. She said two of her aunts and one of her uncles’ individual dwellings were wiped out by the flooding water.

“My mom called me crying and my husband and I were devastated to learn this news,” Moktan said. “My aunt barely made it out of the house, like within three seconds. Then the house was completely swept away.”

According to the U.S. Geological Survey report, the Aug. 26 floods was caused by “a catastrophic debris flow and flood was likely triggered by rapid slope failure involving a glacier in Lāṅṭāṇ National Park, Nepal, near the border with China.”

The floods affected “an estimated 65,000 people, including 22,100 children, across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and Tanahun districts,” a UNICEF USA report said.

The Associated Press reported that at least 1,252 people were killed and more than 4,200 remain missing as of Thursday, according to the country’s disaster management agency. China as of late Wednesday said 21 people were killed and 541 were missing on the Tibet side of the border, according to the Associated Press.

Courtesy of Denisha Moktan Denisha Moktan said 23 of her relatives were left without shelter after three of her family members' homes were washed away. Moktan has started a GoFundMe to assist her family in Nepal. (Courtesy of Denisha Moktan)

Moktan’s mother Kanchhi is one of six siblings that grew up in Trishuli Bazaar in a house next to a bridge over the Trishuli River. Moktan said the bridge was completely “wiped out.”

Moktan said some family members had a close call, including an aunt, uncle and cousin that escaped their doomed in the path of the flooding were able to get out seconds before it was swept away in Trishuli Bazaar.

“They were able to escape with only the clothes on their back and lost their home, belongings and everything they had built,” Moktan said.

Moktan said her cousin received a phone call from a co-worker warning them to seek higher ground minutes before the flood hit. That call likely saved their lives. She added people in town were warned before the flood waters came because updates from others on social media.

“My uncle was a bit stubborn, and he thought they would be the safest in the house,” Moktan said. “But my aunt said ‘No, we need to get to higher ground because the river is taking away houses.’ She grabbed her husband, pushed him and ran. The flood was literally coming behind them. They had an avalanche at their feet. It was pretty harrowing. Especially with the chaos after when everybody was trying to figure out if everybody made it out alive.”

“Then it’s, where do you go? What do you do? There are bodies still washing up. It’s a dire situation. We thank God that our family made it out alive. The government is helping now with food, but we still need help with the shelter portion. I’m working toward building them a house,” she added.

Courtesy of Denisha Moktan A before and after photo the homes destroyed in Nepal on Aug. 26. Family members of Bridgeport resident Denisha Moktan was able to escape to safety but three of her relatives lost homes in the flood. (Courtesy of Denisha Moktan)

Moktan decided to start a GoFundMe to help her family rebuild in Nepal. As of Thursday afternoon, she raised over $12,000 with the goal of about $26,000.

Moktan said her initial plan was to help her family with food, clothes, toothpaste, towels and those essentials, but four days after the flood, the government began distributing food, including bags of rice and cooking oil.

“My family completely lost their homes and livelihood. My uncle was a mechanic and he lost his garage. My other uncle had a clothing store and he lost that. My aunt had a restaurant that is gone. They have no livelihood,” Moktan said.

In all, Moktan has 23 relatives in Nepal impacted by the flooding in Trishuli Bazaar.

Moktan learned that some of her cousins helped save others who were stranded from the flood despite having just lost their own homes. “I was really proud of my family, even though they had lost everything and had nothing. They were helping other families survive,” Moktan said.

She said some of her family members are staying with Moktan’s youngest aunt in Kathmandu, which is about a three-hour drive away.

“I’ve been talking with my aunt, nieces and nephews in Kathmandu,” she said. “Trishuli Bazaar has no access to electricity and no cell tower. Everything is broken. The communication is dead over there.”

Courtesy of Denisha Moktan The family of Bridgeport resident Denisha Moktan in Nepal. This is one of her family's three homes that were destroyed by the Aug. 26 flood. (Courtesy of Denisha Moktan)

Moktan said one of her uncles and a cousin in the Trishuli Bazaar area have been sleeping outside on a towel.

“One night they were sleeping in a temple, but it got too overcrowded. So they were just sleeping outside and hoping it wouldn’t rain. I think the government is working on giving out tents for them to live in,” Moktan said. “There’s no schools or hospitals in that area. Everything was just destroyed. The entire civilization in that area is gone.”

Moktan, 34, spent the first 15 years of her life in Nepal. Since moving to Bridgeport, she has spent summers and holidays in Nepal with family.

“My mom was about 23 when she left Nepal with my dad, but we always went back. That’s my childhood. That’s my childhood memories,” Moktan said. “I was born in Nepal and came to America when I was 15 years old. I worked my way through high school and college. I went to law school and now I’m a tax attorney and I’m grateful for America because none of this would have been possible if I was in Nepal. I had the opportunity from this country. I will never take that for granted.”

Moktan and her mother live 10 minutes away from each other in Bridgeport.

“He will never be able to experience that. It’s all gone,” she said.

Moktan said she has been overwhelmed by the outpouring her family has received with the GoFundMe campaign.

“I’m a little bit taken aback by the outpouring of love and support we have all received from the community on the GoFundMe account. I’ve really been touched. We are hoping to raise about $26,000, which is the cost of a basic house in that area of Nepal,” Moktan said.

“There’s only so much my family can do here,” Moktan added. “I need my community support, so I started the GoFundMe,” she added.

“I’m so touched that people have given what they can. Those who can’t, have reached out to me and tell me that ‘I’m here with you.’ Not everyone is in a situation to give. But those who did, that’s money they could have spent on their family. I will probably never meet them, but having so many people come together, even if they live thousands of miles, is really meaningful,” Moktan said.

Moktan said the tragic flooding in Nepal made her realize “we have to love and cherish who we have while we have them because life is so fragile.”

मोक्तन के जल्दिये पता चललै कि ओकर तीन रिश्तेदार घर त्रिशुली नदी के दौड़-धूप पानि में बह गेलै। ओ कहलनि जे, बाढ़िक पानि मे हुनकर दू टा मौसी आ एकटा काका’क व्यक्तिगत आवास मेटा गेल छल.

मोक्तान कहलनि जे, हमर मम्मी हमरा कानैत फोन केलनि आ हम आ हमर पति ई खबरि सुनि कए तबाह भ गेलहुं। “हमर मौसी मुश्किल स’ घर स’ बाहर निकलि गेलीह, जेना तीन सेकेंड के भीतर।तखन घर एकदम बहरा गेल छल।”

अमेरिकी भूवैज्ञानिक सर्वेक्षण केरऽ रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, 26 अगस्त केरऽ बाढ़ के कारण “एक विनाशकारी मलबा के प्रवाह आरू बाढ़ के शुरुआत संभवतः चीन के सीमा के पास नेपाल केरऽ लांटन नेशनल पार्क म॑ एगो ग्लेशियर के साथ तेजी स॑ ढलान के विफलता के वजह स॑ शुरू होय गेलऽ छेलै ।”

यूनिसेफ यूएसए केरऽ एगो रिपोर्ट म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि बाढ़ स॑ “रासुवा, नुवाकोट, धडिंग, गोरखा आरू तनाहुन जिला भर म॑ २२,१०० बच्चा सहित लगभग ६५,००० लोगऽ प्रभावित होय गेलै ।

देश केरऽ आपदा प्रबंधन एजेंसी के अनुसार, एसोसिएटेड प्रेस केरऽ खबर छै कि गुरुवार तलक कम स॑ कम १,२५२ लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छै आरू ४,२०० स॑ भी अधिक लोग लापता छै । एसोसिएटेड प्रेस के अनुसार चीन बुधवार के देर तक सीमा के तिब्बत तरफ 21 लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छै आरू 541 लोगऽ के लापता होय गेलऽ छै ।

देनिशा मोक्तान के सौजन्य स देनिशा मोक्तान कहलनि जे, हुनकर परिवार के तीन सदस्य के घर बहला के बाद हुनकर 23 परिजन बिना आश्रय के रहि गेल छथि। मोक्तान नेपाल मे अपन परिवार के सहयोग के लेल GoFundMe शुरू केने छथिन्ह. (देनिशा मोक्तान के सौजन्य)

मोक्तान केरऽ मां कांची वू छह भाई-बहिनऽ म॑ स॑ एक छै जे त्रिशूली बाजार म॑ त्रिशूली नदी प॑ बनलऽ पुल के बगल म॑ एगो घर म॑ पललऽ-बढ़लऽ छै । मोक्तान कहलनि जे पुल पूरा तरहे “मिटा” गेल अछि।

मोक्तान कहलनि जे, परिवार के किछु सदस्य के करीबी फोन छल, जाहि मे बाढ़ि के रास्ता मे अपन बर्बाद स बचल एकटा चाची, चाचा आ चचेरा भाई त्रिशूली बाजार मे बाढ़ि के बहय सं सेकेंड पहिने बाहर निकलि सकलाह।

मोक्तान कहलनि जे, ओ सब मात्र पीठ पर कपड़ा ल क भागि सकलाह आ घर, सामान आ बनौने सब किछु गंवा देलनि।

मोक्तान कहलनि जे, हुनकर पितियौत भाई के एकटा सहकर्मी के फोन आयल छल जे बाढ़ि सं किछुए मिनट पहिने हुनका सब के ऊँच जमीन खोजय के चेतावनी देल गेल छल। संभवतः ओ फोन हुनका लोकनिक जान बचा लेलक। ओ इहो कहलनि जे, बाढ़ि के पानि एला सं पहिने शहर के लोक के चेतावनी देल गेल छल किएक त सोशल मीडिया पर दोसर के अपडेट.

मोक्तान कहलनि जे, हमर काका कनेक जिद्दी छलाह, आ हुनका लागल जे घर मे ओ सब सबस सुरक्षित हेताह। “मुदा हमर मौसी बजलीह ‘नहि, हमरा सभ केँ ऊँच जमीन पर पहुँचबाक आवश्यकता अछि किएक त’ नदी घर छीनि रहल अछि।’ ओ अपन पति केँ पकड़ि लेलक, धक्का द’ क’ दौड़लीह। बाढ़ि अक्षरशः पाछू आबि रहल छल। हुनका लोकनिक पैर मे हिमस्खलन भ’ गेल छल। ई काफी दुखद छल। खास क’ ओकर बादक अराजकताक संग जखन सब कियो ई बुझबाक प्रयास मे छल जे सब कियो एकरा जीवित क’ लेलक कि नहि।”

"तखन त’, कतय जायब? की करब? एखनो लाश धो रहल अछि. ई एकटा भयावह स्थिति अछि. हम भगवान केँ धन्यवाद दैत छी जे हमर परिवार एकरा जीवित क’ लेलक। सरकार आब भोजन मे मदद क’ रहल अछि, मुदा हमरा सभ केँ एखनो आश्रय भाग मे मदद चाही. हम हुनका सभ केँ घर बनेबाक दिशा मे काज क’ रहल छी।”

देनिशा मोक्तान के सौजन्य स 26 अगस्त के नेपाल में घर सब तबाह भेल छल। (देनिशा मोक्तान के सौजन्य)

मोक्तान नेपाल मे अपन परिवार के पुनर्निर्माण मे मदद करय लेल GoFundMe शुरू करय के फैसला केलनि. गुरुवार के दुपहर तक ओ करीब 26 हजार डॉलर के लक्ष्य के संग 12 हजार डॉलर सं बेसी के धनराशि जुटा सकलीह.

मोक्तान कहलनि जे, हुनकर प्रारंभिक योजना छल जे ओ अपन परिवार के भोजन, कपड़ा, टूथपेस्ट, तौलिया आ ओहि आवश्यक सामान मे मदद करी, मुदा बाढ़िक चारि दिन बाद सरकार भोजन बांटब शुरू केलक, जाहि मे चावल के थैली आ खाना बनाबय के तेल शामिल छल।

मोक्तान कहलनि जे, हमर परिवारक घर आ रोजी-रोटी एकदम गमा लेलक, हमर काका मिस्त्री छलाह आ हुनकर गैराज चलि गेलनि।हमर दोसर काका के कपड़ाक दोकान छल आ ओ ओ गमा लेलनि।हमर मौसी के रेस्टोरेंट छल जे नहि अछि, हुनका सब के कोनो रोजी-रोटी नहि अछि।

कुल मिला कए त्रिशूली बजारमे भेल बाढ़िसँ प्रभावित नेपालमे मोक्तानके २३ परिजन रहल अछि ।

मोक्तन क॑ पता चललै कि हुनकऽ कुछ पितियौत भाई न॑ दोसरऽ लोगऽ क॑ बचाबै म॑ मदद करलकै जे अभी-अभी अपनऽ घर गंवाय क॑ बाढ़ स॑ फंसलऽ छेलै । ओ कहला जे हमरा अपन परिवार पर सचमुच गर्व छल, भले ओ सब किछु गंवा चुकल छल आ ओकरा लग किछु नहि छल। ओ सब दोसर परिवार कए जीवित रहबा मे मदद क रहल छल।Ó मोक्तान कहला।

ओ कहलनि जे, हुनकर परिवार के किछु सदस्य मोक्तान के छोटका मौसी के संग काठमांडू मे रहैत छथि, जे करीब तीन घंटा के ड्राइव दूर अछि.

ओ बजलीह, “हम काठमांडू मे अपन मौसी, भतीजी आ भतीजा सब स’ गप्प करैत आबि रहल छी। ओ कहला जे त्रिशुली बाजार मे बिजली क सुविधा नहि अछि आ सेल टावर सेहो नहि अछि। सब किछु टूटि गेल अछि। ओम्हर संवाद मरि गेल अछि।”

देनिशा मोक्तान के सौजन्य नेपाल के ब्रिजपोर्ट निवासी देनिशा मोक्तान के परिवार। ई हुनकऽ परिवार केरऽ तीन घरऽ म॑ स॑ एगो छै जे 26 अगस्त क॑ बाढ़ स॑ तबाह होय गेलऽ छेलै । (देनिशा मोक्तान के सौजन्य)

मोक्तान कहलनि जे, त्रिशूली बाजार इलाका मे हुनकर एकटा मामा आ एकटा पितियौत भाई बाहर तौलिया पर सुतल छथि।

“एक राति ओ सभ एकटा मंदिर मे सुतल छल, मुदा ओहि ठाम बेसी भीड़ भ गेल। तेँ ओ सभ बस बाहर सुतल छलाह आ आशा मे छलाह जे बरखा नहि होयत. हमरा लगैत अछि जे सरकार हुनका सभक रहबाक लेल टेंट देबा पर काज क’ रहल अछि।’ मोक्तान कहलनि, ‘ओहि इलाका मे कोनो स्कूल आ अस्पताल नहि अछि। सब किछु बस नष्ट भ गेल। ओहि इलाकाक समस्त सभ्यता खतम भ’ गेल अछि।”

34 वर्षीय मोक्तान अपन जीवनक पहिल 15 साल नेपाल मे बितौलनि। जहिया स ब्रिजपोर्ट आबि गेलीह तहिया स गर्मी आ छुट्टी परिवार क संग नेपाल मे बिता रहल छथि।

ओ कहला जे हमर मम्मी करीब 23 साल क छलीह जखन ओ हमर पापा क संग नेपाल स निकलल छलीह, मुदा हम सब सदिखन वापस जाइत छलहुं। से हमर बचपन अछि। हमर बचपनक याद इएह अछि।’ मोक्तान कहलनि जे, हमर जन्म नेपाल मे भेल छल आ 15 सालक उम्र मे अमेरिका आयल छलहुं। हाई स्कूल आ कॉलेज मे अपन काज केलहुं। हम लॉ स्कूल मे गेल रही आ आब टैक्स अटॉर्नी छी आ अमेरिका’क आभारी छी किएक त’ जँ हम नेपाल मे रहितहुँ त’ एहि मे सँ कोनो काज संभव नहि होइत. हमरा एहि देश स मौका भेटल। हम ओहि बात केँ कहियो हल्का मे नहि लेब।”

मोक्तान आरू ओकरऽ मां ब्रिजपोर्ट म॑ एक-दूसरा स॑ १० मिनट के दूरी प॑ रह॑ छै ।

ओ कहला जे ओ कहियो एहन अनुभव नहि क सकैत छथि। सबटा खतम भ’ गेलै।-ओ बजलीह।

मोक्तान न॑ कहलकै कि गोफंडमी अभियान के साथ हुनकऽ परिवार क॑ जे उफान मिललऽ छै, ओकरा स॑ हुनी अभिभूत छै ।

“हमरा सब क॑ गोफंडमी अकाउंट प॑ समुदाय स॑ मिललऽ प्रेम आरू समर्थन केरऽ बहाब स॑ हम्में कनी चकित छियै । हम त’ सत्ते छू गेल छी। हम सब करीब 26 हजार डॉलर जुटेबाक उम्मीद क रहल छी, जे नेपाल क ओहि इलाका मे बेसिक मकान क लागत अछि।Ó मोक्तान कहला।

मोक्तान आगू कहलकै, “एत’ हमर परिवार एतेक काज क’ सकैत अछि.” ओ आगू कहलनि जे, हमरा अपन सामुदायिक सहयोग चाही, ताहि लेल हम गोफंडमी शुरू केलहुं।

“हमरा ततेक भावुकता अछि जे लोक जे द’ सकैत अछि से द’ देलक अछि. जे नहि क’ सकैत छथि, हमरा लग हाथ बढ़ा क’ कहने छथि जे ‘हम एतय अहाँक संग छी.’ सबहक एहन स्थिति मे नहि अछि जे देब’ पड़त. मुदा जे केलक, से पाइ ओ अपन परिवार पर खर्च क’ सकैत छल. हम शायद कहियो हुनका सब स भेंट नहि करब, मुदा एतेक लोक कए एक ठाम आबि कए रहब, भले ओ हजारों मील दूर रहथि, सचमुच सार्थक अछि।Ó मोक्तान कहला।

मोक्तान कहलनि जे नेपाल मे आयल दुखद बाढ़ि हुनका ई अहसास करा देलक जे “हमरा सभ लग जे अछि ओकरा प्रेम आ पोसय पड़त जखन कि हमरा सभ लग अछि, कारण जीवन एतेक नाजुक अछि।”

title: Elizabeth Shackelford: Nepal’s disaster is today’s terrifying climate change reality - Chicago Tribune
description: Elizabeth Shackelford: Nepal’s disaster is today’s terrifying climate change reality  Chicago Tribune
publisher.title: Chicago Tribune
full_article:
On the morning of Aug. 26, a catastrophic flash flood traveled around 60 miles along the Nepal-Tibet border region, destroying bridges, buildings and a border crossing. It swallowed entire villages and swept thousands of people along with it. Whole tour buses are still missing. More than 1,200 people have been confirmed dead, with thousands more still unaccounted for, including hundreds trapped in the tunnels of hydropower projects.

This shocking event, at the end of a summer when the world was already on fire , was yet another reminder that climate change is no longer a hypothetical threat to our future, but a deadly and ever-present threat that can strike us without warning at virtually any time, anywhere.

No rain was in the forecast. Many videos capturing the racing wall of water revealed blue skies above. Heavy rains can cause raging waters too, but at a rate that people and communities can often respond to. This tragedy offered its victims little time to find safe cover. It was a nightmare come to life.

When it first occurred, the cause was a mystery, but scientists have since established, through before-and-after satellite images, that a 2,000-foot-wide chunk of ice snapped off a glacier at 17,000 feet and fell nearly three-quarters of a mile to the valley floor, triggering a massive landslide and the flood. The crash caused the equivalent of a 4.4 magnitude earthquake. The wave of water moved at an average speed of 120 mph. That means it advanced 14 miles in less than seven minutes.

Those who survived the horrors of the flood are now faced with the long-term struggle to survive in its aftermath with what little of value it left behind. The after scenes are apocalyptic. Buildings are gutted or gone. What was once a lush, green landscape is now broken and painted brown, covered in thick mud and debris.

This disaster was made possible by climate change. Warmer temperatures are melting ice rapidly, destabilizing glaciers that have stood for tens of thousands of years and longer. While that period has seen ice advance and retreat at various times, the speed of melting today has no precedent. Since the 1980s , as global average temperatures have risen, ice melt has dramatically accelerated too. Although the specific tragedy in Nepal was unexpected, massive glaciers make the impact of climate change obvious to the naked eye.

A drone view shows a damaged residential building along the swollen Trishuli River in the aftermath of flash floods in Nepal's Nuwakot district, on Sept. 3, 2026. (Rajesh Kumar Singh/AP)

I’ve seen the scale of that impact firsthand on France’s largest glacier. For two decades, I’ve skied the Vallee Blanche in the Alps, a 14-mile run, considered the longest in the world, that descends the Mer de Glace, a glacier whose name translates to “sea of ice.” The famous ski run ends at the Montenvers Railway, which has carried skiers and sightseers from the end of the glacier back to the village of Chamonix since 1909. Or at least that is what it did before the ice began its rapid retreat. A metal plate marks the spot where the ice reached in 1985, still nearly level with the station built almost 80 years before. In 1988, three steps were added to ease access to the station level as the glacier began to drop. By 1990, 12 steps were required, as it receded at a faster pace. Only 10 years later, 118 steps. By 2015, 321.

The last time I skied the Vallee Blanche two years ago, its beauty and scale were still awe-inspiring, but signs of its decline in the face of a warming world were all around us, dampening our spirits as we wondered about the future, of the Alps and our world. When we reached the end of the glacier, we followed spits of snow across the dirt where the glacier used to be. It was much farther and more challenging than I’d remembered, and when we reached the end of the trail, we had to climb 580 metal stairs up to the station. I was clad in ski boots with skis on my shoulder as I solemnly followed the reverse chronology of the glacier’s retreat. It was a striking visual of just how much and how fast global warming had changed the landscape there. The hike out became so difficult that a new lift was recently installed to bring tourists in and out instead.

Melting glaciers are more than a disappearing tourist attraction in Europe and America. While wealthier countries are often equipped with better tools to detect and respond to climate change-induced crises than poorer ones are, they also face increased risks of landslides, catastrophic floods and rockfall. But you don’t have to be near the glaciers themselves to be affected by them. Melting ice will affect us all, as the water makes its way from mountains to rivers to seas, raising sea levels and altering ocean circulation in ways that will affect populations everywhere.

Some climate change disasters are slow but steady, easy to track but also easy to ignore: rising temperatures of air and water, heat waves that get progressively worse, shrinking lakes and rising seas. Others, such as this flash flood, come fast and furious. What is even more alarming, though are the climate change nightmares we haven’t imagined yet, since we don’t fully understand where the trajectory of rising temperatures will lead.

Elizabeth Shackelford is a foreign affairs columnist for the Chicago Tribune and a lecturer with the Dickey Center at Dartmouth College. She was previously a U.S. diplomat and is the author of “The Dissent Channel: American Diplomacy in a Dishonest Age.”

नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला में, 3 सितम्बर, 2026 के आकस्मिक बाढ़ के बाद सूजल त्रिशुली नदी के किनारे क्षतिग्रस्त आवासीय भवन के ड्रोन दृश्य में देखल गेल अछि।(राजेश कुमार सिंह/एपी)

फ्रांसक सब सं पैघ ग्लेशियर पर ओहि प्रभावक पैमाना हम स्वयं देखलहुं. दू दशक सं हम आल्प्स में वैली ब्लैंच पर स्कीइंग क’ रहल छी, जे 14 मीलक दौड़ थिक, जकरा दुनियाक सब सं नमहर मानल जाइत छैक, जे मेर डी ग्लेस सं उतरैत छैक, जे एकटा ग्लेशियर थिक जकर नामक अनुवाद “ बर्फक समुद्र” होइत छैक. प्रसिद्ध स्की रन मोंटेनेवर्स रेलवे पर समाप्त होइत अछि, जे 1909 सं ग्लेशियरक छोर सं स्कीयर आ दर्शनीय स्थल कें वापस चामोनिक्स गाम धरि ल जा रहल अछि.वा कम सं कम बर्फक तेजी सं पाछू हटब शुरू हेबा सं पहिने ई काज एहने करैत छल. एकटा धातु के प्लेट ओहि जगह के चिन्हित करैत अछि जतय 1985 में बर्फ पहुंचल छल, जे एखनो लगभग 80 साल पहिने बनल स्टेशन सं लगभग समतल अछि. 1988 म॑ तीन सीढ़ी जोड़लऽ गेलै ताकि स्टेशन स्तर प॑ पहुँच म॑ आसानी होय सक॑, कैन्हेंकि ग्लेशियर गिरै लगलै । 1990 तक 12 डेग देबाक जरूरत छल, किया कि इ तेजी स हटि गेल। मात्र 10 साल बाद 118 डेग। 2015 तक 321।

पिछला बेर दू साल पहिने जखन हम वैली ब्लैंच पर स्कीइंग केने रही तं ओकर सुंदरता आ पैमाना एखनो भयभीत करयवला छल, मुदा, गरम होइत दुनियाक सोझां एकर पतन केर संकेत हमरा लोकनिक चारूकात छल, जे भविष्यक, आल्प्स आ अपन दुनियाक बारे में सोचैत काल हमरा लोकनिक मनोबल कें नम क’ दैत छल. जखन ग्लेशियरक छोर पर पहुँचलहुं तं बर्फक थूकक पाछू-पाछू गंदगीक ओहि पार गेलहुं जतय पहिने ग्लेशियर छल. हमरा मोन सं बेसी दूर आ चुनौतीपूर्ण छल, आ जखन पगडंडीक छोर पर पहुँचलहुं तं स्टेशन धरि 580 धातुक सीढ़ी चढ़य पड़ल. हम कान्ह पर स्की ल’ क’ स्की बूट पहिरने रही, जखन हम ग्लेशियरक रिट्रीट’क उल्टा कालक्रमक गंभीरतापूर्वक पालन करैत रही. ई एकटा हड़ताली विजुअल छल जे ग्लोबल वार्मिंग सं ओतय के परिदृश्य कतेक आ कतेक तेजी सं बदलि गेल छल. हाइक आउट एतेक कठिन भ गेल जे हालहि मे एकटा नव लिफ्ट लगाओल गेल अछि जाहि सं पर्यटक के एकर बदला मे अंदर-बाहर आनल जा सकय.

पिघलैत ग्लेशियर यूरोप आ अमेरिका में गायब भ रहल पर्यटक आकर्षण सं बेसी अछि. जहाँ एक तरफ अक्सर गरीब देशऽ के तुलना म॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन स॑ पैदा होय वाला संकटऽ के पता लगाबै आरू ओकरऽ जवाब दै लेली बेहतर उपकरण स॑ लैस होय छै, वहीं ओकरा भूस्खलन, विनाशकारी बाढ़ आरू चट्टान गिरै के खतरा भी बढ़ी जाय छै । मुदा ग्लेशियर स’ प्रभावित होब’ लेल स्वयं ग्लेशियरक लग मे रह’ के जरूरत नहिं. बर्फ के पिघलला स॑ हमरा सब प॑ असर पड़तै, कैन्हेंकि पानी पहाड़ स॑ नदी तलक समुद्र तक के रास्ता बनाबै छै, जेकरा स॑ समुद्र केरऽ स्तर बढ़ी जाय छै आरू समुद्र केरऽ परिसंचरण म॑ ऐन्हऽ बदलाव आबै छै जेकरा स॑ हर जगह के आबादी प्रभावित होय जैतै ।

जलवायु परिवर्तन केरऽ कुछ आपदा धीमा लेकिन स्थिर, ट्रैक करना आसान छै लेकिन ओकरा नजरअंदाज करना भी आसान छै: हवा आरू पानी केरऽ बढ़तऽ तापमान, गर्मी केरऽ लहर जे प्रगतिशील रूप स॑ खराब होय जाय छै, सिकुड़ी जाय वाला झील आरू बढ़तऽ समुद्र । दोसर, जेना ई फ्लैश फ्लड, तेजी सं आ उग्र भ' क' अबैत अछि. मुदा, एहि सं बेसी चिंताजनक बात अछि जलवायु परिवर्तनक दुःस्वप्न जकर कल्पना हमरा लोकनि एखन धरि नहिं केने छी, कारण, हमरा लोकनि कें पूर्णतः ई नहिं बुझल अछि जे बढ़ैत तापमानक प्रक्षेपवक्र कतय जायत.

एलिजाबेथ शैकलफोर्ड शिकागो ट्रिब्यून केरऽ विदेश मामलऽ के स्तंभकार आरू डार्टमाउथ कॉलेज केरऽ डिकी सेंटर के साथ व्याख्याता छै । पहिने ओ अमेरिकी राजनयिक छलीह आ “द डिसेंट चैनल: अमेरिकन डिप्लोमेसी इन ए डिहोनेस्ट एज” के लेखिका छथि ।

title: 2 trapped Nepal hydropower tunnel workers rescued 9 days after devastating floods - CBS News
description: 2 trapped Nepal hydropower tunnel workers rescued 9 days after devastating floods  CBS News
publisher.title: CBS News
full_article:
Kathmandu, Nepal — Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a hydropower tunnel Friday as emergency teams continued an operation to reach others believed to be trapped inside, officials said.

The two men were rescued from the Trishuli 3A tunnel nine days after floods, likely caused by a glacier collapse, devastated towns and swept away villages in Nepal on Aug. 26.

Nepalese lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane posted about the second rescue on his Facebook page shortly after army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet confirmed the first trapped worker's rescue.

CBS News' Ramy Inocencio reports that "there's renewed hope that we might be seeing more survivors come out — possibly dozens more — because rescuers have already heard more voices deeper in those tunnels."

A man who survived is carried on Sept. 4, 2026 by members of a search and rescue team. Nepal Army/Handout via REUTERS

Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told Inocencio in a text message that he's "thrilled" about the two rescues and is "hoping to see more survivors." He said it's unclear how many survivors there are, but with those voices being heard, there are more people alive waiting to be saved and the clock is ticking to get to them.

Rescuers first heard voices from inside the tunnel Friday morning, confirming that people were alive and enabling them to locate the two men, Neupane said.

Local television news channels showed images of the first rescued worker covered in mud and being carried from the site on a rescuer's shoulder. Officials said both men were in stable condition and were flown to a hospital in Kathmandu.

When mechanical foreman Sanjay Shah was pulled out, he said "thank you," but he's been advised not to talk anymore because of his condition, CBS News' Inocencio says.

Amir Maharjan, brother of the other rescued worker, mechanical supervisor Kabir Maharjan, told The Associated Press he "can't explain what we are feeling at the moment. We are just grateful to God." He said the family was on its way to the hospital to see him.

Kabir Maharjan's wife, Hirashova, told CBS News partner network BBC News, "We couldn't properly eat or drink for 10 days. We were very scared. Now we are all happy. We are even crying."

At least 557 workers are missing from the Trishuli 3A hydropower project along the Trishuli River, with about 115 believed to be trapped in the main tunnel, according to the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal.

Rescuers carry a survivor from a tunnel linked to a hydropower station at a location given as Rasuwa district, Nepal, in this image released on Sept. 4, 2026. Nepal Army/Handout via REUTERS

A Nepali energy adviser told Inocencio it's not just a tunnel that goes into the ground next to the Trishuli River but a system of rooms and chambers that snake up and down, and that's where the workers are apparently stuck.

The adviser also told Inocencio that the trapped workers are some of the smartest engineers in Nepal and they probably have been trying to figure their own way out and how to get oxygen so they don't run out of air — the biggest risk.

At least 1,287 people were killed in the floods and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to the country's disaster management agency. China, as of late Wednesday, said 21 people were killed and 541 were missing on the Tibet side of the border.

About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects in Nepal, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in tunnels, according to local authorities.

Prabesh Subedi contributed to this report.

title: Nepal: Two pulled alive from tunnel nine days after floods - DW.com

full_article:
Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a hydropower tunnel Friday, nine days after catastrophic floods swept through the country's border region with China.

Emergency teams are continuing efforts to reach hundreds more believed trapped inside similar tunnels.

The men, identified as mechanical foreman Sanjay Shah and mechanical supervisor Kabir Maharjan, were freed from the Upper Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station's tunnel along the Trishuli River, according to a statement from the office of Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha.

"As long as there is breath, there is hope!" Shrestha said in a statement. "Rescue operations are continuing in all the affected tunnels. Let everyone's efforts and prayers continue. We have not lost hope."

What do we know about the rescue?

Rescuers first heard voices from inside the tunnel Friday morning, authorities said.

The two survivors rescued from the Upper Trishuli 3A hydropower project were flown to Kathmandu Image: Athit Perawongmetha/REUTERS

Video and photos showed Maharjan, 45, pulled from a hole in the ground as bystanders cheered. Images showed him being placed on a stretcher, while Shah, 30, whose face was covered in mud, was carried out on a worker's back to a rescue tent, where army doctors fitted him with an oxygen mask and checked his vitals.

An aide to the energy minister said Maharjan could not move his hands or legs, while Shah's injuries were not considered critical. Both men were flown to a hospital in Kathmandu.

Family members reacted with relief. Amir Maharjan, Kabir's brother, told the Associated Press, "I can't explain what we are feeling at the moment. We are just grateful to god," adding that the family was heading to the hospital to see him.

What is happening at the hydropower project sites?

These were the first successful rescues concerning the hydropower projects along the Trishuli River. Officials say as many as 900 workers remain missing across a number of project sites, with roughly 500 believed trapped in tunnels, according to local authorities.

Nepal floods trap hundreds in hydropower tunnels To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

At the Trishuli 3A project specifically, the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal put the number of missing workers at 557, with about 115 believed trapped in the main tunnel.

Nepal's communication minister, Bikram Timilsina, said officials remained hopeful more survivors would be found: "We are waiting for the rescue of more and more people," he said.

A team of experts coordinating through a WhatsApp group has been guiding rescue crews at the sites, becoming a key tool alongside helicopters and heavy machinery in the search effort.

What is the scale of damage caused by the Nepal floods?

Separately, Nepal's disaster authority estimated the floods caused at least 387.5 billion Nepalese rupees ($2.56 billion, €2.20 billion) in damage to property, housing and infrastructure, Dharma Raj Upreti, chief of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, told Reuters.

He said the first four months of early recovery — including rebuilding roads, setting up temporary shelters, and restoring water and power — would cost an estimated $52.6 million.

"These are estimated amounts. We have calculated this in coordination with different concerned agencies and departments," Upreti said, noting a more detailed assessment would follow. He said Nepal would need to rebuild around 20,000 houses in flood-affected areas, with at least 7,500 destroyed outright.

After Nepal floods, survivors return to ruins of their homes To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The floods on August 26 were triggered by the collapse of a glacier upstream on the Trishuli River that sent a wall of ice, rock and mud through towns and villages near the Nepal-China border.

At least 1,259 people have been killed in Nepal, according to the country's disaster management agency, with more than 5,000 still missing.

China reported 21 deaths and 541 people missing on the Tibet side of the border as of late Wednesday.

अलग-अलग नेपाल के आपदा प्राधिकरण के अनुमान छै कि बाढ़ के कारण संपत्ति, आवास आरू बुनियादी ढांचा के कम स॑ कम ३८७.५ अरब नेपाली रुपया (२.५६ अरब डॉलर, २.२० अरब यूरो) के नुकसान होय ​​गेलऽ छै ।

हुनी कहलकै कि जल्दी ठीक होय के पहलौ चार महीना मँ - जेकरा मँ सड़कौ के पुनर्निर्माण, अस्थायी आश्रय स्थल के स्थापना, आरू पानी आरू बिजली के बहाल करना शामिल छै - मँ अनुमानित 5.26 करोड़ डॉलर के लागत आबै वाला छै ।

उप्रेती नँ कहलकै, "ई अनुमानित राशि छै, हम्में अलग-अलग संबंधित एजेंसी आरू विभागौ के साथ समन्वय करी क एकरौ गणना करलौ छियै।" ओ कहलनि जे, नेपाल मे बाढ़ि प्रभावित इलाका मे करीब 20 हजार घर के पुनर्निर्माण करय पड़त, जाहि मे कम सं कम 7500 घर एकदम सं नष्ट भ गेल।

नेपाल बाढ़िक बाद बचि गेल लोक अपन घरक खंडहर मे वापस आबि जाइत छथि ई वीडियो देखबाक लेल कृपया जावास्क्रिप्ट सक्षम करू, आ HTML5 वीडियो केँ सपोर्ट करय बला वेब ब्राउजर मे अपग्रेड करबा पर विचार करू

26 अगस्त के बाढ़ि के शुरुआत त्रिशुली नदी पर अपस्ट्रीम ग्लेशियर के गिरला सं भेल छल जे नेपाल-चीन सीमा के समीप के शहर आ गाम मे बर्फ, चट्टान आ थाल के देबाल भेजल गेल छल.

नेपालमे कमसँ कम १,२५९ गोटेके मृत्यु भेल देशके आपदा व्यवस्थापन एजेन्सीके अनुसार ५ हजारसँ बेसी अखनो लापता अछि ।

चीन मे बुधदिन देर राति धरि सीमाक तिब्बत कात मे 21 लोकक मौत आ 541 लोक लापता अछि।
